description.summary: A legendary winged humanoid creature reported in Point Pleasant, West Virginia from November 1966 to December 1967. Associated with the Silver Bridge collapse and often considered a harbinger of disaster.
description.full: The Mothman is a cryptid that reportedly appeared in Point Pleasant, West Virginia and surrounding areas between November 1966 and December 1967. Witnesses described a large, man-sized or larger creature with enormous wings and glowing red eyes. The Mothman phenomenon became inextricably linked to the collapse of the Silver Bridge on December 15, 1967, which killed 46 people. This association has led to Mothman's reputation as an omen or harbinger of disaster. The town of Point Pleasant has embraced the legend with a museum, statue, and annual festival.

etymology.origin: The name 'Mothman' was coined by an Ohio newspaper copyeditor in 1966, inspired by the Batman TV series that was popular at the time.
etymology.meaning: Combination of 'moth' (due to wing descriptions) and 'man' (humanoid form)

related_phenomena.name: Thunderbirds
related_phenomena.description: Giant birds of Native American legend

features.description: Large bat-like or bird-like wings, 10-15 foot wingspan
Large, glowing red eyes, hypnotic quality reported
Eyes often described as set in shoulders/chest area
Arms not typically reported; wings may substitute

physical.morphology: Large humanoid figure with massive wings folded against or extending from back. Most distinctive feature is large, luminous red eyes. Body described as muscular, gray or dark in color. Witnesses often note absence of discernible head, with eyes appearing to be set directly in upper body.

abilities.description: Capable of high-speed flight without flapping; estimated 100+ mph
Eyes produce or reflect bright red light visible at distance
Kept pace with cars traveling 100 mph

range.description: Primarily confined to Point Pleasant, West Virginia and Mason County during 1966-1967. Sporadic reports from other locations in subsequent decades.

hotspots.name: TNT Area
hotspots.notes: Primary location of initial sightings; abandoned igloos and dense woods

temporal.seasonal_patterns: Original sightings concentrated in late fall/winter months

origins.cultural_roots: No apparent Native American or earlier folklore for this specific entity in the region.
origins.earliest_accounts: November 12, 1966 - Gravediggers near Clendenin report large brown humanoid figure flying over trees.
origins.folklore_connections: Some researchers connect to Cornish Owlman and Native American Thunderbird traditions.

timeline.significance: Earliest documented Mothman encounter near Clendenin, WV
Most famous sighting; two couples chased by creature at TNT area
Point Pleasant Register reports story; term 'Mothman' coined
Witness reports creature flying alongside his car
46 deaths; sightings largely cease afterward; Mothman linked to disaster
'The Mothman Prophecies' starring Richard Gere brings national attention
12-foot stainless steel statue in Point Pleasant

history.modern_era: Since 1967, Mothman sightings have been sporadic. Point Pleasant has embraced the legend with the Mothman Museum, annual Mothman Festival (since 2002), and the iconic 12-foot statue. Sporadic sighting waves occur, including notable Chicago-area reports in 2016-2017.

notable.name: Scarberry-Mallette Sighting
notable.description: Two couples - Roger and Linda Scarberry and Steve and Mary Mallette - were driving near the TNT area around midnight when they saw a large gray creature with glowing red eyes. The creature had wings folded against its back. When they fled in their car, the creature pursued them at speeds over 100 mph, flying without flapping its wings. They drove directly to the Mason County courthouse to report the incident.

credibility.notes: Foundational Mothman sighting; witnesses maintained account for decades

notable.name: Thomas Ury Highway Sighting
notable.description: Thomas Ury was driving on Route 62 in the early morning when he spotted a large gray figure standing in a field. As he watched, the creature spread its wings and flew straight up into the air. It then circled his car and flew alongside it as he accelerated to over 70 mph. The creature eventually veered off.

factors: No prior knowledge of other sightings
